issue.title: sessions: OpenCode, ZCode and dsh sessions count no tools or skills on the Sessions page
issue.body:
Asked on Discord (Creat.wu): the Sessions page's skill (and tool) counts should cover dsh, OpenCode and ZCode too.

On origin/main (ef6d5ca40) a reader counts a tool or skill through `state.tool` (`internal/sessions/sessions.go`). Who calls it:
- counts skills: Claude Code (`Skill` tool), Alma, Pi/omp (`/skill:` and SKILL.md reads)
- counts tools only: Codex, Cursor, Droid, Hermes, Kimi
- counts neither: OpenCode (`parseOpenCode`, all three stores: v1 `part` table, v2 `session_message`, JSON files), ZCode (shares `parseOpenCode`), dsh (`dsh.go`)

What's needed:
- OpenCode v1 keeps a tool call as a `part` of type `tool` with `tool` and `state.input`; its skill tool is `skill` with `{name}`. v2 (`session_message`) keeps an assistant reply's `content` array; how a tool call sits in it isn't confirmed.
- ZCode and dsh: no real session with a skill call has been looked at yet.
- Per LESSONS, fixtures come from real sessions: a real OpenCode (v1 and v2), ZCode and dsh session in which a skill was used, before the readers are changed.

comments.body:
A tool call and a skill call now count for OpenCode (all three stores: the v1 `part` table, the JSON files under `storage/`, and OpenCode 2's `session_message`), ZCode and dsh.

The cause: `parseOpenCode` in `internal/sessions/opencode.go` read a reply's tokens and its first prompt's parts, never the tool parts of a reply, and `dshCount` in `internal/sessions/dsh.go` skipped `tool/call` events. `state.tool` was never called for these three agents, so `day.Tools`/`day.Skills` stayed empty and the page counted zero.

The branch counts each tool-call part (OpenCode v1's `tool` field, OpenCode 2's content entry `name`), reads the skill out of a skill tool's input (`name` in OpenCode's own tool, `id` in the OpenCode 2 sessions on this machine, `skill` in ZCode's `Skill`), counts dsh's `tool/call` events with the skill named in their arguments, and bumps `cacheVersion` to 23 so parses kept by older magpies are read again. Fixtures are the shapes those apps' own sessions have, taken from real ones here (OpenCode 2's `opencode.db`, ZCode 3.14.3's `cli/db/db.sqlite`, a dsh `session.v4.jsonl.zstd`).

[fix/2569-sessions-opencode-zcode-and-dsh](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2569-sessions-opencode-zcode-and-dsh), commit 8b9246b244240c69b441bac0457c785321b9b995

Run: the tests that fail on the old code are `TestOpenCodeFiles`, `TestOpenCodeDB`, `TestOpenCodeV2`, `TestZCode` and `TestDsh` ("opencode tools [] skills []" and the same for zcode and dsh); they pass with the change, as does `go test ./internal/sessions/ -count=1` (669 passed), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/sessions/` and a `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/sessions/`. `go test ./...` has 7 packages red (agent, edit, gateway, plugin, provider, testenv, tui), and every failing test there fails the same way on clean upstream/main.

This is a fork branch ready for review; it makes no claim on the issue.
